facts.fact: The Minister of the Interior says civil status acts are made on secured printed forms ordered by the Ministry of Finance and produced abroad, with a recurring shortage of them, and that the France-backed civil registration modernisation project has drawn up standard civil status forms and a national mapping of the system; the interview gives no date, so its published date is used.
facts.system: état civil (imprimés des actes d'état civil)

systems.system: Projet d'Appui à la modernisation de l'état civil
systems.country_label: projet d'Appui à la modernisation de l'état civil
systems.owner: Ministère de l'Intérieur, in collaboration with France
systems.tiers: Standard forms and a national mapping of the civil registration system produced; 54 communes named as the municipal tier

systems.system: Biometric passports and national identity cards (Semlex, then Genkey)
systems.owner: Ministère de l'Intérieur; Genkey replacing Semlex from 1 April 2026
systems.tiers: Biometric capture on Ndzuani and Mwali, printing on Ngazidja only

note: The paper fact rests on the minister's account of printed forms; he does not say in terms that registration is on paper only.
